output.summary: NOV reported revenues of $1.25 billion and a net loss of $115 million for the first quarter of 2021, marking a 6% sequential decline in consolidated revenue. The company faced significant challenges, including severe winter weather in Texas and Oklahoma, which led to the closure of 63 facilities, and pandemic-related disruptions to supply chains for raw materials like fiberglass and resin. Additionally, execution issues on a new pipe design project and delays on an offshore platform component project contributed to higher costs. Despite these obstacles, NOV slightly exceeded its March forecast due to progress on cost reductions and early signs of recovery in the oilfield, particularly in Wellbore Technologies. The segment saw a 11% sequential revenue increase to $413 million, with seven out of eight business units posting growth. NOV expects Wellbore Technologies revenue to grow 8% to 10% in the second quarter. The Completion & Production Solutions segment reported a 20% sequential revenue decline to $439 million and an EBITDA loss of $4 million, though it achieved a book-to-bill ratio of 127%. NOV anticipates a 15% to 25% sequential revenue improvement for this segment in the second quarter. The Rig Technologies segment generated $431 million in revenue, a 1% sequential decline, with EBITDA of $13 million and a book-to-bill ratio of 59%. NOV began manufacturing rigs from its new plant in Saudi Arabia and is pursuing over $400 million in potential offshore wind projects. The company has reduced costs by $12.6 billion since 2014 and expects to achieve $106 million in cost savings for 2021. NOV ended the quarter with $1.61 billion in cash and $1.85 billion in gross debt, having fully redeemed $183 million of senior notes due in December 2022.
